paper: Egan et al. 2020 (JAC 75:1704-1711; PMID 32129849) - Linezolid resistance in E. faecium and E. faecalis from Irish hospitals, high prevalence of optrA and poxtA

open_questions.q: What is the actual optrA-plasmid transmission topology across the livestock-food-human reservoir chain, and can the Irish clinical optrA-plasmid backbones (represented by MN831410 / pM17/0149, ~99.997% identical to pE394 KP399637) be traced to specific pig, poultry, or retail-meat reservoirs?
open_questions.basis: Egan et al. report near-identical 36,331 bp optrA plasmids (pE394-lineage) in 8 unrelated Irish clinical isolates. pE394 was originally described in E. faecalis of animal/food origin (Wang 2015). Because the paper deposited neither raw reads nor livestock-comparator sequences and provided no plasmid MLST beyond the pE394 identity claim, the clinical-vs-animal transmission direction is unresolved from the deposited artifacts (C5-adjacent, untestable here).
next_steps: Query NCBI Pathogen Detection / EnteroBase for all deposited optrA-carrying enterococcal plasmids (livestock, food, human) and cluster by full-length plasmid ANI against pE394/MN831410
Run mash-screen of MN831410 vs European livestock optrA read-sets (SRA) to place the Irish clinical backbone in a source-attribution tree
Cross-reference with the EFSA/ECDC 2019-2023 zoonotic-AMR surveillance datasets for pE394-lineage isolates by country/host
Contact authors for the 154-isolate metadata (Table S1) linking isolate-ID -> patient exposure history (livestock contact, hospitalisation route)

open_questions.q: What are the fitness / evolutionary trade-offs of optrA vs cfr(D) vs poxtA co-carriage, and does the observed rarity of triple carriage (only 1 optrA+cfr(D) and 1 poxtA+G2576T isolate in the Egan cohort) reflect a genuine selective cost or under-sampling?
open_questions.basis: Egan et al. observed exactly ONE optrA + cfr(D) co-carrier (MN831413, 103,600 bp plasmid confirmed here) and ONE poxtA + 23S G2576T co-carrier out of 35 gene-positive isolates. This looks like negative epistasis (mutual exclusion) but n=35 is under-powered to distinguish a fitness cost from a stochastic cohort effect; no growth-competition assays or transcriptomic data were reported.
next_steps: Meta-analyse published enterococcal genome collections (NCBI Pathogen Detection, >100k enterococcal genomes) for optrA/cfr(D)/poxtA co-carriage frequencies vs single-gene baselines; compute observed-vs-expected ratios under Hardy-Weinberg-style independence
Design head-to-head fitness assays (in vitro competition, +/- sub-inhibitory linezolid) between isogenic optrA-only, cfr(D)-only, poxtA-only, and co-carrier constructs in E. faecium ST80 background
RNA-seq under linezolid pressure to test whether co-carriage induces overlapping ribosome-protection stress responses
Structural modelling of ribosome binding-site occupancy by OptrA/PoxtA (both ABC-F proteins) to test if simultaneous binding is sterically prohibited

open_questions.q: What is the true optrA/poxtA prevalence in COMMUNITY vs HOSPITAL enterococcal isolates in Ireland (and Europe more broadly), and is the 22.7% headline representative of clinical LRE only or of the wider community reservoir?
open_questions.basis: The Egan et al. denominator of 154 isolates is exclusively from patients referred to the Irish National MRSA Reference Laboratory (i.e. hospitalised, already flagged as linezolid-resistant). There is no community-carriage arm and no non-selective baseline. The 22.7% figure therefore describes a maximally-enriched clinical population, not community prevalence. This replication cannot address the gap (C5 untestable).
next_steps: Design a paired community-carriage screen: rectal/stool swabs from healthy Irish community controls (n>=500) with the same optrA/poxtA PCR panel used by Egan et al.
Systematic review + meta-analysis of hospital-vs-community optrA/poxtA prevalence across published European enterococcal surveys 2018-2025
Retrospective screen of banked EARS-Net enterococcal isolates for optrA/poxtA using the Egan primer panel
Petition the HPSC (Health Protection Surveillance Centre, Ireland) to add optrA/poxtA to the national AMR surveillance denominator, not just to LRE-reflex testing

open_questions.q: Under what conditions does optrA integrate into the enterococcal chromosome via IS-element-mediated capture versus being maintained on the pE394-family plasmid, and does chromosomal integration correlate with plasmid loss under de-selection?
open_questions.basis: Egan et al. note optrA both on plasmids AND within the chromosome, but only three hybrid-assembled plasmid contexts (MN831410/13 + variants MN831414-19 as CDS-only regions) were deposited. The chromosomal-integration contexts are described in text but NOT deposited as annotated contigs (the replication caught this: 6 of the 8 optrA-carrying deposited records are CDS-region excerpts, not full flanking contexts). The plasmid-to-chromosome dynamics therefore remain hypothesized rather than tracked.
next_steps: Request from authors (or re-sequence Irish LRE bank) full chromosomal contigs flanking chromosomal-optrA isolates, resolve IS1216E / Tn6674-family transposon boundaries
In vitro passage experiments: pE394-optrA-carrying E. faecium ST80 passaged +/- linezolid, monitor chromosomal-integration frequency by long-read sequencing at timepoints
Comparative genomics: align all publicly deposited chromosomal-optrA E. faecium/faecalis contigs to identify recurrent integration hotspots and the flanking IS element(s) responsible
Test whether chromosomal integrants show lower conjugation-transfer frequency (loss of horizontal spread) as the trade-off for vertical stability

open_questions.q: Does linezolid MIC correlate quantitatively with optrA copy number and/or expression level across the Egan et al. cohort, and what is the MIC contribution of optrA sequence variants (the 6 distinct alleles this replication confirmed)?
open_questions.basis: Egan et al. report cohort-level MIC ranges but do not link isolate-level MIC to optrA/poxtA copy number or to the specific optrA variant carried. The replication confirmed 6 distinct optrA alleles across 8 records (nt-diff vector {0,1,2,2,2,3,6,6} vs canonical NG_048023) but cannot go further because per-isolate MIC-to-accession linkage and raw-read coverage data are not deposited (C7-adjacent).
next_steps: qPCR of optrA copy number in the Irish LRE isolate bank, regress log(MIC) vs log(copy_number), report slope + 95% CI
RT-qPCR of optrA transcript abundance +/- linezolid induction, test whether variant alleles differ in inducibility
Site-directed mutagenesis to reconstruct the 6 optrA variants in an isogenic background, measure MIC of each
Publish an aligned isolate-ID -> MIC -> optrA-variant -> copy-number table (the closure of Egan Table S1 + Table S2 that the paper did not provide machine-readably)
